title: Push Day A
guide: Complete straight sets in order. Rest 90–120 sec after compound lifts and 60 sec after accessories. Leave 2–3 good reps in reserve. When every set reaches the top of its range with good form, add the smallest available load. Start with 2 sets if new to lifting.
warmup: 5–10 min easy movement, then lighter practice sets of the first exercise.
cooldown: 3–5 min easy walking and relaxed breathing.

When every set reaches the top of its range with good form, add the smallest available load. For assisted pull-ups, reduce assistance instead. Start with 2 sets if new to lifting.
warmup: 5–10 min easy movement, then lighter practice sets of the first exercise.
cooldown: 3–5 min easy walking and relaxed breathing.

title: Core Day A
guide: Work slowly and breathe throughout. Rest 30–45 sec between sets. For each-side movements, do both sides before checking a set; enter reps or seconds for one side. Choose a range you can control without back or hip discomfort.
warmup: 3–5 min easy walking, then a few gentle pelvic tilts.
cooldown: 3–5 min easy walking and relaxed breathing.

title: Core Day B
guide: Work slowly and breathe throughout. Rest 30–45 sec between sets. For each-side movements, do both sides before checking a set; enter reps or seconds for one side. Choose a range you can control without back or hip discomfort.
warmup: 3–5 min easy walking, then a few controlled bodyweight hinges.
cooldown: 3–5 min easy walking and relaxed breathing.

title: Mobility Day A
guide: Move slowly through comfortable ranges. Do both sides before checking a set; enter the amount for one side. Rest about 15 sec as needed. Do not force end range. Begin holds at 10 sec if needed, building toward the listed target.
cooldown: 1–2 min relaxed breathing; finish feeling comfortable.

title: Mobility Day B
guide: Move slowly through comfortable ranges. Do both sides before checking a set; enter the amount for one side. Rest about 15 sec as needed. Do not force end range. Begin holds at 10 sec if needed, building toward the listed target.
cooldown: 1–2 min relaxed breathing; finish feeling comfortable.

exercises.name: Adductor Rock-Back
cues: Start on hands and knees; extend one leg sideways with foot supported.
Keep your back steady and gently rock hips backward.
Use a small comfortable range; repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch
cues: Place hands against a wall and step one foot behind you.
Keep the back heel down and lean forward gently.
Hold without bouncing; switch legs.

title: Stability Day A
guide: Quality before load. Use a wall or sturdy support when balance is challenging. Rest 30–45 sec. Do both sides before checking each set; log one side. Stop the set when posture or control breaks down.
warmup: 3–5 min easy walking and gentle ankle movements.
cooldown: 3–5 min easy walking and relaxed breathing.

exercises.name: Supported Single-Leg Balance
cues: Stand beside a wall or sturdy chair and keep fingertips on it as needed.
Lift one foot slightly; keep hips level and eyes forward.
Hold steadily, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
cues: Walk beside a wall or counter for support.
Place each heel just ahead of the toes of the other foot.
Take slow small steps while looking ahead.

title: Stability Day B
guide: Quality before load. Use a wall or sturdy support when balance is challenging. Rest 30–45 sec. Do both sides before checking each set; log one side. Stop the set when posture or control breaks down.
warmup: 3–5 min easy walking and controlled bodyweight hinges.
cooldown: 3–5 min easy walking and relaxed breathing.

exercises.name: Supported Single-Leg Hinge
cues: Use one hand on a stable support and soften the standing knee.
Hinge at the hips as the other leg moves gently behind you.
Keep hips square and return tall; begin without weight.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Abduction
cues: Hold a stable support and stand tall.
Move one leg a little out to the side without leaning.
Return slowly; keep toes facing forward.

title: Cardio Day A
guide: Six different main movements, excluding warm-up and cooldown. Do the 5 min opening movement, then 3 min at each of the next five stations, in the listed order. Keep effort moderate, around 4–6/10, and be able to speak in full sentences. Take extra transition time as needed; start with shorter blocks if needed.
warmup: First block includes a 5 min warm-up.
cooldown: 20 min of main work plus 5 min warm-up and 5 min cooldown; allow time to change stations.

exercises.name: Easy Walking Warm-up
cues: Walk slowly on level ground.
Let breathing and stride settle.

exercises.name: Brisk Walking
cues: Walk at a steady purposeful pace.
Stay tall with relaxed shoulders; use the talk test.

exercises.name: Steady Marching
cues: March in place with relaxed arm swings.
Keep an even pace that still allows full sentences.

exercises.name: Step Touch
cues: Step sideways and bring the other foot toward it.
Repeat in both directions with soft knees and relaxed shoulders.

exercises.name: Heel Digs
cues: Alternate tapping each heel forward.
Keep the supporting knee soft and swing arms gently.

exercises.name: Standing Knee Lifts
cues: Stand tall and alternate lifting one knee at a time.
Stay controlled; use a sturdy support if needed.

exercises.name: Low Step-ups
cues: Use a low, stable step and place the whole foot on it.
Step up and down at a steady pace, changing the lead leg halfway.

exercises.name: Gentle Walking Cooldown
cues: Slow your walking pace gradually.
Let breathing ease toward normal.

title: Cardio Day B
equipment: Gym · bike, rower, elliptical, treadmill, stairs, ski erg
guide: Six different main movements, excluding warm-up and cooldown. Do the 5 min opening movement, then 3 min at each of the next five stations, in the listed order. Keep effort moderate, around 4–6/10, and be able to speak in full sentences. Take extra transition time as needed; start with shorter blocks if needed.
warmup: First block includes a 5 min warm-up.
cooldown: 20 min of main work plus 5 min warm-up and 5 min cooldown; allow time to change stations.

exercises.name: Easy Cycling Warm-up
cues: Set the saddle so the knee stays slightly bent at the bottom.
Pedal easily with light resistance.

exercises.name: Steady Cycling
cues: Maintain a comfortable steady cadence.
Use moderate resistance and a pace that allows full sentences.

exercises.name: Steady Rowing
cues: Set a light-to-moderate rowing resistance.
Drive through legs, then lean slightly and pull; reverse that order to return.

exercises.name: Elliptical Training
cues: Stand upright with feet supported on the pedals.
Use smooth strides at a comfortable moderate effort.

exercises.name: Incline Walking
cues: Choose a manageable treadmill incline and natural walking pace.
Use the safety clip and avoid hanging on the handrails.

exercises.name: Stair Machine
cues: Start at a low speed and keep feet well supported on each step.
Stand tall; use the rails only for light balance support.

exercises.name: Ski Erg
cues: Stand with soft knees and a light resistance setting.
Hinge gently and pull handles down; return smoothly without jerking.

exercises.name: Easy Cycling Cooldown
cues: Reduce resistance and pedal gently.
Let breathing settle before stopping.

title: HIIT Day A
equipment: Gym · bike, elliptical, low stable step
guide: Six different work exercises, excluding warm-up and cooldown. After warming up, finish the six intervals at the first station; then do one interval at each of the five additional stations. Work at a controlled hard effort around 8/10, never an all-out sprint. Take the full 90 sec easy recovery after every work interval, including when changing stations. Reduce interval count or shorten work periods when starting. Use 1–2 non-consecutive HIIT days per week. Log work seconds only and check an interval after recovery.
warmup: Warm-up and cooldown are included as logged blocks.
cooldown: 11 × (30 sec hard + 90 sec easy) = 22 min, plus 10 min warm-up/cooldown. Allow extra time to change stations.

exercises.name: Easy Cycling Warm-up
cues: Pedal easily for 5 min, gradually raising your cadence.
Include a few short moderate efforts near the end if comfortable.

exercises.name: Bike Intervals
cues: Increase resistance or cadence for 30 sec at a controlled hard effort.
Then pedal very easily for 90 sec; recover fully before the next effort.
Complete 6 rounds, or begin with 4.

exercises.name: Fast Marching
cues: March briskly with quick, controlled arm swings.
Keep steps light; avoid leaning back as knees lift.

exercises.name: Step Jacks
cues: Step one foot sideways as arms move outward, then return.
Alternate feet briskly without jumping; keep shoulders in a comfortable range.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing
cues: Keep a soft stance and punch the air without weights.
Alternate controlled punches without snapping elbows straight or twisting knees.

exercises.name: Fast Low Step-ups
cues: Use a low stable step, placing the whole foot on it.
Choose quick but controlled steps and switch the lead leg halfway.

exercises.name: Elliptical Intervals
cues: Increase cadence or resistance for the work period while staying upright.
Then lower the effort for the full recovery period.

exercises.name: Easy Cycling Cooldown
cues: Reduce resistance and pedal easily for 5 min.
Let breathing return toward normal.

title: HIIT Day B
equipment: Gym · treadmill, rower, air bike, ski erg, ropes
guide: Six different work exercises, excluding warm-up and cooldown. After warming up, finish the six intervals at the first station; then do one interval at each of the five additional stations. Work at a controlled hard effort around 8/10, never an all-out sprint. Take the full 75 sec easy recovery after every work interval, including when changing stations. Reduce interval count or shorten work periods when starting. Use 1–2 non-consecutive HIIT days per week. Log work seconds only and check an interval after recovery.
warmup: Warm-up and cooldown are included as logged blocks.
cooldown: 11 × (45 sec hard + 75 sec easy) = 22 min, plus 10 min warm-up/cooldown. Allow extra time to change stations.

exercises.name: Easy Walking Warm-up
cues: Walk easily for 5 min, building to a comfortable purposeful pace.
Use the safety clip; practise adjusting speed and incline first.

exercises.name: Incline Walking Intervals
cues: Raise incline to reach a controlled hard walking effort for 45 sec.
Reduce incline and walk easily for 75 sec. Allow time for belt adjustments.
Keep a natural stride; lower the incline if you need to hang on the rails.

exercises.name: Rowing Intervals
cues: Row strongly with legs first, torso next and arms last.
Keep technique smooth rather than chasing the highest stroke rate.

exercises.name: Air Bike Intervals
cues: Set the seat for a slightly bent knee at the bottom.
Use coordinated arm and leg action for a controlled hard effort.

exercises.name: Ski Erg Intervals
cues: Use a light enough setting to keep the stroke smooth.
Drive handles down with a small hinge and soft knees; avoid jerking your back.

exercises.name: Lateral Shuffle
cues: Use a clear non-slip space and start in a soft athletic stance.
Take short side steps without crossing feet; slow before changing direction.

exercises.name: Battle Rope Waves
cues: Keep a stable stance with soft knees and relaxed shoulders.
Make small alternating waves without shrugging or leaning back.

exercises.name: Gentle Walking Cooldown
cues: Return to a low incline and gradually slow the pace for 5 min.
Let breathing settle before stepping off.
